PRESCRIPTION: 1) Topical steroids (corticosteroids), 2) Vitamin D analogs (calcipotriene), 3) BIOLOGICS for severe (IL-17, IL-23 inhibitors), 4) Phototherapy (UV light). TRIGGERS: Stress, infections, cold, alcohol. See dermatologist - needs medical treatment!

qa_database.question: Can makeup cause acne?
qa_database.answer: YES, if: 1) NOT REMOVED properly (clogs pores overnight), 2) Comedogenic ingredients (coconut oil, certain silicones, heavy oils), 3) Old/expired (bacteria growth), 4) Dirty brushes/sponges (bacteria), 5) Sharing makeup (bacteria transfer). PREVENT: 1) Non-comedogenic products, 2) REMOVE fully (double cleanse), 3) Clean brushes weekly, 4) Replace every 6-12 months, 5) Let skin breathe (no makeup days), 6) Primer + setting spray (barrier). BEST: Mineral makeup (less comedogenic). Skincare > makeup for clear skin!

qa_database.question: How to treat maskne (acne from face masks)?
qa_database.answer: MASKNE (acne mechanica from masks): Friction + moisture + bacteria. PREVENT: 1) CLEAN MASK: Wash cloth masks daily, change surgical masks, 2) BREATHABLE fabric (cotton, silk), 3) WELL-FITTING (not too tight), 4) Barrier cream (zinc oxide, Aquaphor) before mask. TREAT: 1) Gentle cleanser after removing mask, 2) Salicylic acid 2% OR benzoyl peroxide 2.5%, 3) Lightweight moisturizer, 4) Hydrocolloid patches on active pimples. AVOID: Heavy makeup under mask. Worse in healthcare workers - rotate mask areas if possible.

qa_database.question: What causes skin tags and how to remove them?
qa_database.answer: SKIN TAGS: Small, soft growths (friction, genetics, hormones). Common: neck, armpits, groin, eyelids. HARMLESS. CAUSES: 1) Friction (skin rubbing), 2) Genetics, 3) Pregnancy (hormones), 4) Obesity, 5) Diabetes, 6) Aging. REMOVAL: 1) DERMATOLOGIST: Surgical scissors, cryotherapy (freezing), electrocautery (burning), 2) AT-HOME: OTC freeze kits, tag removal devices (risky - infection, scarring). DON'T: Cut yourself, tie with string (infection risk!). Insurance usually doesn't cover (cosmetic). Prevention: Reduce friction, maintain healthy weight.

qa_database.question: What is the best anti-aging ingredient?
qa_database.answer: TOP ANTI-AGING INGREDIENT: RETINOIDS (retinol, tretinoin). WHY: 1) PROVEN in clinical studies (gold standard), 2) Increases collagen, 3) Speeds cell turnover, 4) Fades dark spots, 5) Smooths texture, 6) Reduces wrinkles. CLOSE SECOND: SUNSCREEN (prevents 80% of aging - not treatment but crucial!). OTHERS (supportive): Vitamin C (antioxidant), peptides (collagen signal), niacinamide (multi-purpose), AHAs (exfoliation). BEST ROUTINE: SPF daily + retinoid nightly = most effective anti-aging duo. Nothing beats this combination!

qa_database.question: How to get rid of milia (tiny white bumps)?
qa_database.answer: MILIA: Tiny white cysts (trapped keratin under skin). Common around eyes, cheeks. CAUSES: 1) Heavy creams (especially eye area), 2) Sun damage, 3) Trauma/burns, 4) Genetics. TREATMENT: 1) PROFESSIONAL EXTRACTION (dermatologist/esthetician - safest), 2) Regular use of AHA/retinol (prevents, doesn't remove existing), 3) Chemical peels (professional). DON'T: Pick, squeeze, poke (scarring, infection!). PREVENT: 1) Lightweight eye creams, 2) SPF, 3) Regular exfoliation (AHA 2-3x/week). Takes time - be patient, don't DIY extract!

qa_database.question: What is the skin microbiome and how to protect it?
qa_database.answer: SKIN MICROBIOME: Trillions of bacteria/fungi/viruses living on skin (mostly beneficial!). FUNCTIONS: 1) Protects from pathogens, 2) Supports barrier, 3) Regulates inflammation, 4) Maintains pH. IMBALANCE = acne, eczema, rosacea, sensitivity. PROTECT: 1) DON'T over-cleanse (2x/day max), 2) Gentle pH-balanced cleansers (5-6), 3) AVOID harsh antibacterials (kills good bacteria), 4) PREBIOTICS/PROBIOTICS in skincare (feed good bacteria), 5) Limit antibiotics. EMERGING: Microbiome-friendly skincare. Balance = healthy skin!

qa_database.question: What are the signs of aging skin?
qa_database.answer: AGING SIGNS: 1) WRINKLES/FINE LINES (forehead, crow's feet, smile lines), 2) LOSS OF FIRMNESS/SAGGING (jowls, neck), 3) VOLUME LOSS (hollow cheeks, temples, under eyes), 4) DARK SPOTS/UNEVEN TONE (sun damage), 5) ENLARGED PORES, 6) DRYNESS, 7) CREPEY TEXTURE, 8) DULLNESS, 9) BROKEN CAPILLARIES, 10) THINNER SKIN. TIMELINE: 20s = fine lines start, 30s = loss of collagen, 40s = sagging/volume loss, 50s+ = significant changes. SLOW IT: SPF, retinoids, antioxidants, healthy lifestyle from 20s!

qa_database.question: What is the best skincare routine for beginners with no experience?
qa_database.answer: COMPLETE BEGINNER ROUTINE: START SIMPLE (Week 1-4): MORNING: 1) Gentle cleanser (CeraVe Foaming or Hydrating), 2) Moisturizer (CeraVe Moisturizing Lotion), 3) Sunscreen SPF 30+ (Neutrogena Clear Face). EVENING: Same cleanser + moisturizer. WEEK 5-8: Add ONE treatment serum (niacinamide 5% OR vitamin C 10%). WEEK 9-12: Add retinol 0.25% 2x/week evening. SLOW + STEADY! DON'T: Start 10 products at once, change products weekly, skip SPF. BUDGET: ~$50 total. SIMPLE = sustainable = results!

qa_database.question: How to know if a product is working?
qa_database.answer: SIGNS PRODUCT WORKS: POSITIVE: 1) Skin feels hydrated (moisturizer), 2) Breakouts decrease (acne treatment - 6-8 weeks), 3) Texture smooths (exfoliants, retinol - 4-8 weeks), 4) Dark spots fade (brightening - 8-12 weeks), 5) Fine lines soften (retinol - 12+ weeks), 6) No new sun damage (SPF). NEUTRAL (not working): No change after appropriate time. NEGATIVE (bad reaction): Redness, burning, rash, new breakouts in different areas - STOP! TIMELINE: Give 8-12 weeks minimum (2-3 skin cycles) before judging. Track with photos!

qa_database.question: Should I use different products for day and night?
qa_database.answer: YES, optimize for different needs: MORNING (protect): 1) Lighter cleanse, 2) ANTIOXIDANTS (vitamin C - fights daytime damage), 3) Lightweight moisturizer, 4) SUNSCREEN (essential!). EVENING (repair): 1) Thorough cleanse, 2) TREATMENTS (retinol, AHA/BHA - work overnight), 3) Richer moisturizer, 4) NO SUNSCREEN needed. DIFFERENT because: Retinol = sun-sensitive, Vitamin C = boosts SPF, Night = repair mode. CAN SIMPLIFY: Same cleanser + moisturizer okay. Key differences: SPF (AM only), retinol (PM only), vitamin C (AM better).

qa_database.question: What causes forehead acne?
qa_database.answer: FOREHEAD ACNE causes: 1) HAIR PRODUCTS (oils, silicones, heavy conditioners touching forehead), 2) HATS/HEADBANDS (friction, sweat), 3) HORMONES, 4) Touching face/leaning on hands, 5) Stress, 6) Digestive issues (forehead = traditional Chinese medicine mapping). TREAT: 1) KEEP HAIR OFF FACE (especially sleeping), 2) Non-comedogenic hair products, 3) Salicylic acid 2%, 4) Benzoyl peroxide, 5) Clean hats/headbands, 6) Retinol. WORST: Heavy pomades, coconut oil hair masks. Tie hair back while sleeping!

qa_database.question: What causes chin and jawline acne?
qa_database.answer: CHIN/JAWLINE ACNE: Usually HORMONAL! CAUSES: 1) HORMONES (period, PCOS, birth control changes), 2) Touching/leaning on chin, 3) Phone (bacteria), 4) Mask wearing. CHARACTERISTICS: Deep, cystic, flares around period. TREATMENT: 1) SPIRONOLACTONE (prescription for women - anti-androgen), 2) Birth control pills (regulate hormones), 3) Topical retinoids, 4) Benzoyl peroxide, 5) Clean phone regularly. AVOID: Dairy (may worsen hormonal acne). See dermatologist if persistent - topicals alone often insufficient for hormonal acne!

qa_database.question: How to treat under-eye bags and puffiness?
qa_database.answer: UNDER-EYE BAGS: CAUSES: Aging (fat pads shift), genetics, fluid retention, allergies, lack of sleep. TREATMENT: TOPICAL (minimal): 1) CAFFEINE eye cream (constricts vessels, reduces fluid), 2) Cold compress/ice, 3) Jade roller (refrigerated). PROFESSIONAL (effective): 1) FILLERS (tear trough - lifts sagging, $700-1200), 2) BLEPHAROPLASTY (eye surgery - removes fat bags, permanent), 3) Laser (tightens skin). LIFESTYLE: 1) Sleep elevated, 2) Reduce salt, 3) Allergy meds if applicable. REALISTIC: True bags = structural, need professional treatment.

qa_database.question: What is the best way to apply skincare products?
qa_database.answer: APPLICATION TECHNIQUES: CLEANSER: Massage 30-60 seconds, rinse. TONER: Pat with hands (better than cotton - less waste). SERUM: 3-4 drops, pat/press into skin (don't rub aggressively). EYE CREAM: Ring finger (gentlest), dot + pat, don't pull. MOISTURIZER: Dime size, warm in hands, press in upward motions. SUNSCREEN: 1/4 teaspoon face, dot then blend. GENERAL: 1) Gentle pressure (no tugging), 2) Upward motions (anti-gravity), 3) Pat > rub (better absorption), 4) Wait 1-2 mins between layers. NECK: Upward strokes.

qa_database.question: Does washing face with cold water shrink pores?
qa_database.answer: MYTH! Cold water does NOT shrink pores (they can't open/close - no muscles!). WHAT COLD WATER DOES: 1) Temporarily CONSTRICTS blood vessels (less redness), 2) Feels refreshing/tightening (temporary). WHAT ACTUALLY MINIMIZES PORES: 1) Salicylic acid (unclogs), 2) Retinol (thickens surrounding skin), 3) Niacinamide (regulates oil), 4) Clay masks. BEST WATER TEMP: LUKEWARM for cleansing (removes dirt without stripping). Hot = strips oils, Cold = can't clean as well. Finish with cool rinse if like the feel!

qa_database.question: How often should I change my pillowcase?
qa_database.answer: PILLOWCASE: Change/wash 1-2x PER WEEK (minimum weekly). WHY: 1) Oils from hair/face accumulate, 2) Dead skin cells, 3) Bacteria (causes breakouts), 4) Product buildup. BEST: 1) SILK/SATIN (less friction = less wrinkles + frizz), 2) Cotton (breathable if not silk), 3) Have 2-3 sets (rotate). ACNE-PRONE: Change every 2-3 days. ALTERNATIVE: Flip pillowcase (fresh side) mid-week. ALSO CLEAN: Sheets weekly, wash with fragrance-free detergent. Simple habit = better skin + hair!

qa_database.question: What is face yoga and does it prevent wrinkles?
qa_database.answer: FACE YOGA: Facial exercises claiming to tone muscles, reduce wrinkles. THEORY: Exercises strengthen facial muscles = lifted, firmer skin. EVIDENCE: Limited scientific proof, small studies show minor improvement. CONCERN: Repeated facial movements may CREATE wrinkles (why Botox works by preventing movement!). SAFER ALTERNATIVES: 1) Facial massage (lymphatic drainage), 2) Gua sha, 3) Proven treatments (retinol, SPF, Botox). VERDICT: May help circulation/relaxation, unclear if prevents wrinkles, possibly counterproductive. Better: sleep on back, SPF, retinol, minimize expressions.

qa_database.question: What is LED light therapy for skin?
qa_database.answer: LED LIGHT THERAPY: Different wavelengths treat skin concerns. TYPES: 1) RED (630-700nm): Boosts collagen, reduces wrinkles, healing, 2) BLUE (400-470nm): Kills acne bacteria, reduces oil, 3) YELLOW (570-590nm): Reduces redness, inflammation, 4) GREEN (520-560nm): Hyperpigmentation, calming. DEVICES: At-home (less powerful, $100-300) vs Professional (stronger, dermatologist). SESSIONS: 3-5x/week, 10-20 mins. RESULTS: Subtle, gradual (8-12 weeks). SAFE, non-invasive. BEST FOR: Acne (blue), anti-aging (red). Supplement to routine, not replacement for actives!

qa_database.question: What is the best routine to fade acne scars fast?
qa_database.answer: FAST SCAR FADING (still takes 8-12 weeks!): MORNING: 1) Gentle cleanser, 2) VITAMIN C 15-20% (brightens PIH), 3) NIACINAMIDE 5-10% (evens tone), 4) Moisturizer, 5) SPF 50+ (CRUCIAL - sun darkens scars!). EVENING: 1) Cleanser, 2) RETINOL 0.5-1% or Tretinoin 0.05% (speeds cell turnover, fades pigment), 3) Moisturizer. 2-3X/WEEK: AHA exfoliant (glycolic 10%). FASTER: 1) Hydroquinone 4% (prescription), 2) Professional peels, 3) Laser. PATIENCE! No instant fix. Consistency = results.

qa_database.question: Can I use expired skincare products?
qa_database.answer: DEPENDS: THROW OUT: 1) Sunscreen (loses efficacy - skin cancer risk!), 2) Acne treatments (benzoyl peroxide, retinoids - oxidize), 3) Vitamin C serum (oxidized = brown/orange color), 4) Products with weird smell/color/texture, 5) Mascara/liquid eyeliner (bacteria). OKAY (if look/smell fine): Basic cleansers, moisturizers 6-12 months past expiry. CHECK: 1) PAO symbol (jar with number = months after opening), 2) Expiration date, 3) Changes in smell/color/separation. STORAGE: Cool, dark place extends life. When in doubt, toss it! Safety > saving money.
